What we do

Insurance companies do not always pay the full amount that may be recoverable for out-of-network services. We identify claims that may be eligible for Independent Dispute Resolution and manage the process from start to finish, including:

  • Reviewing claims for IDR eligibility
  • Identifying underpaid claims worth pursuing
  • Initiating and managing open negotiation
  • Filing eligible claims for IDR
  • Preparing and submitting the IDR case
  • Managing applicable deadlines
  • Tracking determinations and payments
  • Following up on unpaid awards

Your team continues its normal billing process. We handle the IDR process.

How it works

Six steps, each with its own deadline. We run all of them.

  1. 1Day 0

    Remittance review

    Every payment file is screened for claims processed under the No Surprises Act.

  2. 2Before filing

    Eligibility check

    Plan type, facility, consent, and forum are confirmed. Ineligible claims are set aside, not filed.

  3. 3Within 30 business days

    Open negotiation

    We send the required notice and negotiate toward a fair settlement.

  4. 4Within 4 business days

    Filing and batching

    Disputes are filed on time, with similar claims grouped into batches of up to 50.

  5. 5About 30 business days

    Offer and evidence

    Each offer is backed by training, case complexity, and the plan's own past rates.

  6. 630 calendar days

    Collection and reporting

    Awards are tracked until paid. You get a clear statement of every claim.

Who we serve

Federal IDR can apply to certain out-of-network services subject to the No Surprises Act, including services commonly provided by the specialties below. Eligibility depends on the particular claim, payer, plan, service and circumstances.

Anesthesiology

Groups covering hospitals and surgery centers where they are not contracted with every plan.

Radiology

High-volume reads, batched by plan and code so smaller claims are worth disputing.

Pathology and labs

Specimens from in-network facilities, plus New York referral claims.

Emergency, surgical, and hospital-based

Emergency physicians, surgeons, assistant surgeons, and hospital-based specialists.

Air ambulance

Out-of-network air transport is protected under the No Surprises Act.

Facilities

Out-of-network emergency facility claims at hospitals and freestanding ERs.

Federal and New York, handled together

The patient's plan decides where a dispute belongs. A claim filed in the wrong system is dismissed, so we sort every claim before filing.

Questions

Short answers to what practices ask most.

Does this affect my patients?
No. The patient's share is fixed at their in-network amount before any dispute begins. The dispute is only between the provider and the plan.
Which claims qualify?
Emergency care, care by out-of-network providers at in-network hospitals, outpatient departments, critical access hospitals and surgery centers, and air ambulance. Commercial coverage only. Medicare, Medicaid, and Medicare Advantage are excluded.
How do your fees work?
Nothing upfront. Our fee is a percentage of the additional amount recovered above the insurer's initial payment, set in a written agreement.
How long does it take?
IDR is a deadline driven process that begins shortly after the insurer’s initial payment or denial. We monitor the applicable deadlines and move eligible claims through open negotiation, IDR submission, determination and payment follow-up. Actual timing varies depending on the claim, insurer and IDR entity.
What can we recover?
The insurer’s initial payment does not necessarily determine the ultimate reimbursement. Through IDR, providers may be able to recover additional reimbursement above the amount originally paid by the insurer. Results vary by claim, and no particular recovery is guaranteed.
Can you work on older claims?
Only claims still inside their deadlines. The free review shows which windows are open and which have closed.
Do you replace our billing company?
No. We work alongside your billing team, using the remittances they already receive.
What do you need from us?
Getting started is simple. We generally need claims and remittance data, EOBs or ERAs showing the insurer’s payment, basic information regarding the service provided, and authorization to manage the IDR process on your behalf. We review the data to identify claims that may qualify and determine which claims make economic sense to pursue.
